summary: Master time management and priority execution with practical tools, workload tracking, and stakeholder-ready planning.
lede: Time and priority management training helps professionals with active workloads sort competing demands and turn commitments into a workable plan. Participants learn to assess how time is used, rank tasks with methods such as the Eisenhower Matrix and MoSCoW, protect focus through time-blocking, and decide what to delegate based on capacity while communicating priority and deadline conflicts clearly.
audienceIntro: This course is for professionals who already manage active workloads and need stronger control over priorities, interruptions, and delivery commitments.
prerequisites: You need a laptop, access to spreadsheet software, and a willingness to use your own task list, calendar, and recurring work examples during exercises. No coding is required, and advanced software setup is not necessary, although familiarity with digital calendar and task tools will help.
